newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 5.0/5.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 5.0/5.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 5.0/5.5 percent on Monday morning on the back of sustained ample liquidity, dealers said.
They said the market was flush, but longer-term money was well bid as operators prepared for the new reserve requirement rate of five percent from April 16.
One local bank dealer said short-term liquidity was well supplied as reflected by the rates, but the underlying sentiment suggested some worries for Tuesday.

"Tax payments are traditionally high during the last week of the fiscal year," the dealer said, adding Thursday offers the last opportunity as the market will be closed on Friday for a public holiday. The market will also be closed for book closing on Monday due to the fiscal year-end.
One- and three-month money were quoted at 10.75/11.00 and 12.50/12.75 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 4.68 percent, compared with 5.22 percent on Thursday.
Bond dealers said the market remained buoyant, with the yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond edging down to 14.625 percent at the last done price of 107.50 percent.
"We sold quite a lot at 107.5 percent on Friday. Demand seems to be sustained at present," one leading bond dealer said.
Another said some interest was also seen in the new issue of the 250 billion rupiah convertible bonds of PT Muliasentra Gunaswakarya, a property investment company.
